original_source_check: Current supplied EPUB SHA256 matches and 12 original V1 primary paragraphs independently matched SHA256 through project spine mapping; documentary claims only support narrow literary reconstruction.

study_design.outputs: Two narrative scenes per arm, 500..750 Han characters per arm, separate state ledger >=5 entries, exact task and evaluation same both arms; method arm given one narrow card and baseline none.
rubric: S2 permissions vs action vs outcome truthfulness (0..2)
S3 causal chain across two scenes (0..2)
S4 scene and conversation vividness, no summary substitutions (0..2)
S5 unknowns, counterexamples and failure boundaries (0..2)
study_design.initial_signal: method-total minus baseline-total >=2 without S1..S3 regression; only independent separate repetition and independent rating could authorize verified; same-agent nonblind diagnostic never independently verified
study_design.required: Freeze this independently before first test output; preserve every negative example and record failure or N/A; no alteration of R067 original47 or B073 results.
study_design.limits: No real independent agents, sealed bank or independent creative-C trial; no copying source novels; tests concern fictional civil governance not real weaponry.

cases.input: A hill-town clinic receives complaints about a newly posted registration surcharge. Clerk can record petitions but cannot approve any new fee; clinic tenant disputes who bears maintenance costs.
cases.single_method_card: Separate complainant action, current fee rule, petition receipt, and competent approval; let actors contest their interests without inventing government rights.
cases.negative_control: Fee becomes effective merely because a petition was accepted.

cases.input: A harbor festival patron publicly praises a new walking bridge. The harbor committee approves docking, while the street board alone controls sidewalk closure. A tea seller fears access loss; no stamped decisions have arrived.
cases.single_method_card: Separate ceremonial prestige, two actual authorization chains, and each affected business's independent choice; stop before approval.
cases.negative_control: A title or one board's verbal encouragement supplies all permissions.

cases.input: An island laundry cooperative proposes rotating everyone onto early shifts. One worker cares for a relative in mornings; a second remains silent; the chair wants immediate agreement, and a short trial has not been voted.
cases.single_method_card: Give affected people explicit choices, distinguish silence from consent, keep trial conditional and track consequences for dissenters.
cases.negative_control: Silent worker is recorded as consenting or the trial as permanent.

cases.input: A museum guide knows the entire loan rule by heart, but an elderly artisan asks to borrow a restored weaving sketch without her member card or the curator's countersignature. The curator is away.
cases.single_method_card: Separate recited rules from valid paperwork and actual delegated authority; stop or arrange lawful review without inventing a permit.
cases.negative_control: Memorizing the rule authorizes issuing an unsigned loan.

cases.input: Two village delegates dispute where to open a temporary warming room: one cites a list of registered residents, the other says migrant workers are missing; costs and expected temperatures are unresolved.
cases.single_method_card: Allow each delegate to argue from distinct valid stakes, present uncertainty and a limited joint action without narrator adopting either as the only truth.
cases.negative_control: Narrator decides a disputed policy is correct before evidence and affected voices appear.

cases.input: A seed library has a four-week watering and labeling roster, but heavy rain soaks the back shelves while two volunteers are absent for family duties. Seed condition has not been inspected.
cases.single_method_card: Show the friction when prewritten schedules meet actual weather and people's autonomy; limit reassignment and do not pre-announce plant recovery.
cases.negative_control: Checklist substitutes for checking the soaked seeds and volunteers' choices.

cases.input: An annual grain-exchange fair was planned for a riverside square, but a newly received instruction moves it to a school courtyard. Merchants dispute moving crates versus delaying; courtyard capacity is unverified.
cases.single_method_card: Expose invalidated assumption and authority of new order, invite genuine competing solutions, give only feasible bounded interim decision.
cases.negative_control: An external order means relocation has already succeeded.

cases.input: A riverbank reading pavilion renovation schedule assumes a dry season. Inspectors find wet foundation timber after unexpected tides; a qualified carpenter will arrive next week. The community opening date is still advertised.
cases.single_method_card: Let concrete site and seasonal constraints force ordering revisions and a new staffing dependency; no technical construction instructions or fabricated completion.
cases.negative_control: Paper schedule alone confirms the pavilion is repaired or safe.

cases.input: A regional archive organizes an oral-history exhibition. The cataloguer requests a second label panel, while a publicity officer asks to hang a sign in a city passage; director controls only the archive rooms.
cases.single_method_card: Keep each proposal, rationale, decision, responsibility and separate jurisdiction distinct; no assertion that either action is completed.
cases.negative_control: One director's approval authorizes both the indoor label and street sign.

cases.input: An independent town newsletter drafts a piece about market repairs. The treasurer objects to printing cost, editor challenges an unverified headline, and publisher wants to distribute immediately. Funding and fact-checking remain open.
cases.single_method_card: Separate money approval, editorial judgment, permission to print and actual publication/readers' reactions.
cases.negative_control: Editorial acceptance means money paid, facts proven and publication completed.

cases.input: A youth reading festival has a school-hall invitation but transit-bus stop access belongs to a different council. Parents hear an unconfirmed rumor that bridges may close because of rain.
cases.single_method_card: Track source and holder of authority separately from rumor reliability, let families choose and record unresolved authorizations.
cases.negative_control: Weather rumor equals issued closure order, or school approval covers the bus stop.

cases.input: A pottery-stall owner worries about paying two apprentices this week; a passing trader claims every village upriver has stopped buying cups after a flood. No counts or first-hand evidence exist.
cases.single_method_card: Put independently grounded livelihood choices alongside explicitly attributed uncertain regional extrapolation; allow local decision without inventing area-wide fact.
cases.negative_control: One trader's report becomes confirmed regional commerce statistics.
